bounds: evidence/n3-vulkan-timing-bounds.json (written 394285a, addendum A bdce706, both before any run)
code: feat/n3-vulkan-timing at bdce706: Window::refreshHz (Win32 display configuration, Wayland wl_output.mode), the Vulkan swapchain's VK_GOOGLE_display_timing refresh, refresh_hz and refresh_source in the run and pacing records

t1_refresh_windows.observed: D3D12 on WARP: refresh_hz 60, source swapchain. Vulkan on SwiftShader (Win32 surface): refresh_hz 60, source window. Equal on the same monitor. Hidden windows, Idle priority, 10 frames each.
t1_refresh_windows.note: SwiftShader does not offer VK_GOOGLE_display_timing, so the Vulkan value came from the window's copy of the display-configuration function; the two copies agree.

t2_refresh_linux_ci.observed: lavapipe in the vulkan-linux CI job (run 38981280448): X11 on Xvfb refresh_hz 0, source none; Wayland on headless Weston refresh_hz 60, source window. Neither surface got a value from the swapchain, so lavapipe does not offer display timing there.

t3_rtx_vulkan_queued.why: It needs the GPU lock (held by MMBU FT8) and the author's agreement to a borderless fullscreen window for about three minutes on the machine in use. The job script is prepared (mission-control, not in the repository) and not launched.

does_not_prove: Pacing on Vulkan hardware or on a Steam Deck; HDR10 through a Vulkan swapchain; that any compositor presents at the reported rate. A refresh value is what the system reports, not a measurement of presents.
